title: Overtaking & Being Overtaken
whatItIs: Overtake only when it's safe and legal, give vulnerable road users at least as much room as a car, and never obstruct someone who is overtaking you.
keyFacts: Before overtaking, check the road ahead is clear, nobody is starting to overtake you and there's a gap to return to.
Mirrors, signal, a quick glance into the blind spot, then move out. Pass quickly and don't cut in.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT overtake if you would cross or straddle double white lines with the solid line nearest you.
You MUST NOT overtake after a 'No Overtaking' sign, or the vehicle nearest a pedestrian crossing.

keyFacts: Overtake on the left only if the vehicle in front is signalling to turn right and there's room.
Being overtaken: keep a steady course and speed. If they cut in, drop back to a two-second gap.

visual.caption: Guide clearances (rule 163): if you can't give them, wait behind

items.label: Overtaking cyclists at up to 30 mph
items.note: Give more space at higher speeds

a.label: Law: MUST NOT overtake (rule 165)
points: Double white lines with the solid line nearest you
Into a bus, tram or cycle lane during its hours
After a 'No Overtaking' sign, until the end sign
Into a hatched area bordered by a solid white line

b.label: Advice: do not overtake (166–167)
points: Approaching a bend, hump bridge or brow of a hill
At or approaching a junction on either side
When a road user is signalling right
Where you would force someone to swerve or slow

onTheTest.question: Your pupil is following a cyclist on a 30 mph road. As a guide, what is the minimum space to leave when overtaking?
onTheTest.why: Rule 163: leave at least 1.5 metres when overtaking cyclists at speeds of up to 30 mph, and more at higher speeds. If you can't, wait behind.

onTheTest.question: Double white lines are solid on your side. A horse rider ahead is going at 8 mph and the road is clear. What does the Highway Code allow?
options: You may never cross a solid white line
You may cross the lines to pass, if it's safe
You may cross only if the rider waves you on
You may cross only on a straight road
onTheTest.why: Rule 129: you may cross to overtake a pedal cycle, horse or road maintenance vehicle at 10 mph or less, if the road is clear. Pass wide and slow: at least 2 m (rule 215).

traps: Don't just follow a vehicle that is overtaking: there may only be room for one.
A right signal ahead that 'should have been cancelled'? Don't overtake: wait for it to be cancelled.
Cutting in after overtaking is a DT1 judgement fault: move back left as soon as you can, but don't cut in.
Large vehicles: drop back to see ahead and so the driver can see you in their mirrors.
